about: Every number here is computed from the records committed under docs/results by backend/bench/report.py, and a test fails if this file and the records disagree.

headline.claim: Throughput and queue wait at 1, 2 and 4 workers, and what limits them
headline.value: 89.0 → 177.8 → 336.6 tasks/min at 1, 2, 4 workers (3.76×); median queue wait 24.4 → 11.9 → 6.0 s
headline.detail: The bottleneck, measured: the host's CPUs. At 4 workers they were 93.3% busy, 98% of it the workers' own agent loops and sandboxed commands; 8 workers did 0.98× the work of 4, with a runnable task waiting for a CPU 89.1% of the time against 5.5%.

sections.title: Scaling on one host
sections.config: one virtualized host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 4 logical CPUs, 15.72 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.18.44-fc-v51, Python 3.13.12; every process — the fleet workers, its api, PostgreSQL 16 and the bench — on that one host, not a cluster; 72 jobs a batch (the 18-task set four times, seed 1), every pool's trials interleaved with the order reversed every other trial; commit f74eb39, clean checkout
points: The bottleneck, measured: the host's CPUs. At 4 workers they were 93.3% busy, 98% of it the workers' own agent loops and sandboxed commands; 8 workers did 0.98× the work of 4, with a runnable task waiting for a CPU 89.1% of the time against 5.5%.
At the model's recorded latency the CPUs were 49.1% busy at 16 workers; the loss there was the batch's own tail, 13.6% of the workers' time idle after their last job while the longest jobs finished.
In containers a job cost 2.65 CPU-seconds at 4 workers against 0.80 in a worker's own process, and 16 workers kept the CPUs 93.6% busy.

sections.title: Fault injection
sections.config: 260 runs: 26 scenarios × 10 seeds; 230 runs of 30 jobs on 3 worker processes, 20 runs of 18 jobs on 3 worker processes, 10 runs of 18 jobs on 5 worker processes; 1 s leases, 5 attempts per job; the workers, the api and a local PostgreSQL on one virtualized host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 4 logical CPUs, 15.72 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.18.44-fc-v50, Python 3.13.12; commit b64c1fd, clean checkout; every scenario also runs in CI on every push
points: 450 kills, 150 dropped connections, 110 pauses and hangs, 30 Postgres restarts. After every run the checker reads the database back: exactly one result per job, nothing lost, no stale write, accounting that adds up; 740 of 740 planned faults happened, and every one left the effects it must.
There is no scheduler process to restart: workers pull, and Postgres holds all state, so the api is killed mid-request and Postgres is restarted instead.

points: One sentence added to the agent's system prompt, run against the real model with and without it. Replayed from its own recorded responses, each arm's trial came out the same job for job: 18 of 18 without the sentence, 18 of 18 with it.

Expectations met: 100.0% of runs without the change, 100.0% with it, a change of +0.0 points (95% interval +0.0 to +0.0) over 18 paired runs of 18 jobs. 0 met it only with the change and 0 only without (exact McNemar p = 1.000, counting each paired run on its own): no detectable change.
Tokens per job: 6,552 → 3,510 tokens (-3,041, -46.4%; 95% interval -5,533 to -1,105): better.
Cost per job at the pinned price: 0.00853 → 0.00436 USD (-0.00417, -48.9%; 95% interval -0.00721 to -0.00179): better.
Model calls per job: 5.17 → 4.11 calls (-1.06, -20.4%; 95% interval -1.78 to -0.50): better.
Time waiting on the model per job: 5.17 → 2.69 s (-2.48, -48.0%; 95% interval -3.78 to -1.35): better.
Service time per job: 57.45 → 28.62 s (-28.83, -50.2%; 95% interval -45.24 to -13.36): better.
